text:
alex: Quick thought — we should add a `stability_tier` to rollout metadata, not just TTL. TTL doesn't capture semantic quality like 'experimental' vs 'stable'.
maya: +1. How would that affect the resolver? We'd need mapping to `fallback_priority` so clients prefer stable variants.
sam: If we add `stability_tier` we also need to version the schema. Make it optional with default 'unknown' so older clients don't break.
kim: Also capture `compat_hash` (runtime compatibility fingerprint) and `runtime_profile` so Dedicated/Private can auto-select compatible kernels.
alex: Draft manifest snippet: 
```
{
  "model_id": "rwd/llama-70b-qlora",
  "version": "2026-03-14",
  "stability_tier": "staged",
  "fallback_priority": ["staged","stable","legacy"],
  "compat_hash": "sha256:abcdef...",
  "grace_window_secs": 3600
}
```
maya: Looks reasonable. Ops concern: older runtimes must ignore unknown fields. Runtime should tolerate and fallback gracefully.
sam: Runtime patch is pretty small: unknown fields get ignored and we map `stability_tier` to soft weights. Biggest lift is telemetry + Console UX to surface tiers.
jordan: Can we add `gating_signals` array for server-side checks (latency/quality regressions) that can automatically demote a model if thresholds are hit?
alex: Yes but restrict scope: automatic demotion allowed only in Hosted/Dedicated; Private deployments can configure local policies. We should not allow arbitrary remote policies to affect other tenants.
kim: Also recommend `traffic_fraction_rollout` baked into the manifest so rollout is a single source of truth: 
```
"traffic_fraction_rollout": {"steps": [{"after_secs":0, "fraction":0.05}, {"after_secs":86400, "fraction":0.2}], "max_fraction": 0.5 }
```
maya: Document semantics: fractions apply after tenant-level overrides and must respect tenant caps. Console should show effective expected traffic.
sam: Migration plan idea: publish schema v2 behind a feature flag. Console + SDK opt-in. Server responds with header `X-Model-Meta-Schema: v2` for canary clients.
alex: Ops-bot: can we run a lint job to flag manifests missing `compat_hash` or `stability_tier` for prod-tagged models? Prefer failures -> warnings depending on env.
ops-bot: scheduled job created: `model-manifest-lint` every 6h; will open pager for prod models missing `compat_hash`.
jordan: Security/abuse note: don't give clients raw `fallback_priority` arrays. Expose an opaque `fallback_token` that server resolves to an order to avoid client-side gaming and to keep freedom to change priorities.
maya: Good call. Lets keep the public surface minimal; expand only when necessary.
kim: Action items: 1) RFC PR with manifest v2 diff + examples (alex), 2) runtime change list + compatibility tests (kim), 3) Console mocks + telemetry mapping (maya), 4) API docs + migration playbook (sam).
alex: I'll open the PR tomorrow with schema diff and compatibility notes.
maya: Will draft Console mock by EOW.
sam: I'll prototype server header behavior and add unit tests.
kim: I'll start runtime patch and add parsing tolerant tests.
jordan: I'll write short playbook for private deployments describing how to opt into auto-demotion signals.
alex: Thanks all — syncing on this again Friday.
